key_facts: On Oct. 13, 2023, Best Buy emailed that it had received Plaintiff's application for General Warehouse Worker / 2nd Shift at $22.60, requisition 928556BR. On Oct. 17 at 3:47 p.m., Jose Tapia, General Manager, emailed a congratulations offer for that job and required, within 24 hours, Candidate Zone signature, background-check information, and background-check authorization; California disclosure PDFs were attached but are not in this upload. At 4:22 p.m. Best Buy sent a background-authorization confirmation naming First Advantage Consumer Center. At 4:30 p.m. First Advantage ordered a Best Buy drug test (Q09078711; account BEST BUY 11759586; Quest Modesto listed as a collection option). At 5:31 p.m. Best Buy HR reminded him to complete the screen and wrote 'Congratulations on accepting your offer' — that sentence is their characterization, not a Candidate Zone audit. No pre-adverse letter, adverse letter, drug-test result, signed offer, or warehouse street address is in the file. The complaint does not attach a Best Buy report and does not allege its contents as a known fact. The load-bearing theory is information-and-belief use of § 290.46 disclosures. Supporting inference: written offer, same-day First Advantage screen, contemporaneous registry listing, and First Advantage's July 2024 UPS report matching this Plaintiff to the California registry — same vendor, same Plaintiff, methodology and matchability, not Best Buy transmission. Civ. Code §§ 1786.10 / 1786.22 inspection has not yet been demanded.
procedural_status: Verified complaint review draft, demurrer-hardened, generated for proposed September 8, 2026 execution; deliberately unsigned and unfiled. The draft pleads that a court cannot run Lerma on an unattached Best Buy report and that ICRAA § 1786.40 is an independent path against a named CRA. Pre-execution gates: (1) confirm what the employment decision was and its date; (2) confirm whether Plaintiff signed the offer or completed the drug test; (3) confirm the warehouse city; (4) confirm no pre-adverse or adverse package arrived; (5) verify current California agents for Best Buy Co., Inc. and First Advantage Background Services Corp.; (6) execute on or after September 8 only after those confirmations. Three years from Oct. 17, 2023 is Oct. 17, 2026 if that week is accrual. No CRD charge. No demand. Filing court is San Joaquin Superior Court. Companion Judicial Council forms are not yet generated. Arbitration policy is recited in the Oct. 13 application email; the policy itself is not in the upload.
damages: The offer states $22.60/hour for General Warehouse Worker / 2nd Shift. It does not state weekly hours or a start date. Portfolio valuation is $0 until the decision, hours, and Best Buy report are documented. Contingent statutory remedies if use is proven: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) actual/treble with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty capped at $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater. Do not import UPS/Pilot numbers.
risk: Stronger paper than Home Depot: written offer, $22.60, requisition, and a named CRA. Still no rejection letter and no Best Buy report. Lerma dismissed after the employer's report was in the record — a demurrer cannot replicate that analysis while Best Buy and First Advantage withhold the report. If production later shows court records and no California-registry source, the 290 count dies then; ICRAA § 1786.40 can still reach discovery. Best Buy will move to compel arbitration based on the application-email recital; that is a defense, not a claim. Diversity removal is likely. Do not invent a worksite city from the Modesto collection-site option.
